newsitem.title: UK: POLL-UK Labour seen marginally ahead on Europe.
newsitem.headline: POLL-UK Labour seen marginally ahead on Europe.

text.p: The British opposition Labour party is credited with having a safer pair of hands on the country's relations with Europe than the ruling Conservatives, a Reuters/NOP opinion poll showed on Monday.
The exclusive poll showed that 33 percent of respondents would trust Labour most to manage Britain's relations with Europe, against 29 percent who thought the Conservatives would do better.
Fifteen percent thought that there was nothing to choose between any of the parties, while 17 percent said they did not know.

Labour's showing is slightly better than six weeks ago, when the same question was asked in a previous Reuters poll. Then, 34 percent said they trusted Labour most to manage Britain's sometime stormy relationship with its European partners, with 31 percent saying they would prefer to leave it to the Conservatives.

Europe is yet to make much of an impact on the British election campaign, with most voters saying in polls that education, social services, unemployment or simply the need for a change after 18 years of Conservative government were their principal concerns.
But both parties traded accusations at the weekend of incompetence and inconsistency over the handling of Britain's proposed entry into European currency union.

The poll of 1,088 people across 52 constituencies was taken on Friday, before Labour's foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook made what Conservatives said was a U-turn on Labour's policy over Britain's entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Cook said that if a Labour government did not take Britain into EMU at its scheduled starting date of January 1, 1999, it would be unlikely to do so in the course of the next parliament, which can run a maximum of five years.
The Conservative party, trailing Labour badly in all opinion polls, has adopted a "wait-and-see" policy on EMU entry.
Both parties have pledged to hold a referendum before any final decision is made on joining the single currency club.
